description:
ANANTRA is a team of curious and ambitious enthusiasts passionate about space exploration, technology and innovation. We aim to turn challenging ideas into meaningful solutions using AI, software engineering, data science and creative problem-solving.
We're looking for passionate individuals interested in Python, web development, 3D modelling, data analysis and scientific research.
If you're curious and ready to build something extraordinary, join ANANTRA Let's explore beyond the known!
summary:
ANANTRA is a web-based Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that turns astronaut training into a hands-on journey for young learners. Cadets enrol with a privacy-first local profile, study 10 spaceflight lessons with interactive diagrams, and then operate four simulators: a real-time Moon landing, a Zero Gravity Lab, a spacewalk repair and an orbital emergency drill. They can also ask ARIA, an offline-first AI mentor, questions. Progress earns XP and ranks, and six mastery-gated certificates can be exported as PDFs.

This answers the challenge by making astronaut missions something students do rather than just read about. It matters because early, engaging STEM experiences build curiosity and confidence. ANANTRA needs no account, install or API key, so it works in any browser, including classrooms. Lesson facts are grounded in NASA educational resources and honestly separated from the simplified simulations.
details:
What it does and how it works
ANANTRA follows a training path: Cadet Onboarding, Dashboard, six training modules, simulators and quizzes, XP and progress, then a certificate.

  • Onboarding: the cadet picks a name, callsign and astronaut specialization (Lunar Explorer, Mars Pioneer, Space Station Specialist or Cosmic Scientist). Age group, avatar and favorite destination are optional.
  • Astronaut Academy: 10 lessons covering orbits, rockets, the Moon, Mars, spacesuits, the ISS, the human body and radiation. They include interactive diagrams, NASA mission case studies and a 10-question mastery exam.
  • Mission Control: a real-time Moon landing under lunar gravity (1.62 m/s²). It has Cadet and Commander modes and a four-metric landing score.
  • Zero Gravity Lab: compares motion with and without friction, shows astronaut recoil, and demonstrates water surface tension in microgravity.
  • Spacewalk Training: a pre-EVA safety-tool check, then a four-stage truss repair on a limited oxygen reserve.
  • Emergency Training: triage of three orbital alerts while keeping a Station Safety meter above the pass level.
  • ARIA AI Mentor: offline Q&A across 10+ topics, three-step progressive hints, telemetry debriefs and a 5-question quiz. An optional Cloud AI button calls a serverless endpoint and falls back to offline mode if it isn’t configured.
  • Certificates: six mastery-gated certificates with unique IDs, exportable as A4 vector PDFs, printable, and verifiable against local records. Ticking checklist boxes alone does not earn one.

Benefits and intended impact

  • Learners get hands-on practice with immediate feedback instead of passive reading.
  • Teachers and families can use it with no account, cost or setup, so it runs on school computers and phones.
  • Age-aware onboarding (under 10 to 17+) and a progression of XP, ranks and certificates keep learners motivated.
  • Our goal is to spark curiosity about space careers and build early physics intuition, such as gravity, inertia, life support and decision-making under pressure.

Tools and technologies

  • React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8 and Tailwind CSS v4
  • Framer Motion for animation, jsPDF for certificate export, Vitest for testing
  • Hosted on Vercel, with an optional serverless endpoint (/api/mentor)
  • Hardware: none beyond a standard web browser
  • Development approach: AI-assisted development using Antigravity, by a beginner team of six

NASA data and resources (stated transparently)
The current version does not call NASA APIs. Lesson facts and simulation constants are grounded in NASA educational resources from NASA Science, Space Place, Glenn Research Center and nasa.gov. They are listed in the app’s References page. Examples are lunar gravity, ISS orbit facts and microgravity as continuous free-fall. Future work includes NASA open APIs (such as Astronomy Picture of the Day) and mission datasets.

Creativity

  • Education is framed as astronaut training, with ranks, specializations and certificates.
  • Simulators are paired with lessons and mentor hints.
  • Certificates are tied to real mastery.
  • The app states where its models simplify reality, in a References page that compares real spaceflight with the classroom model.
  • ARIA works offline first, so classroom use doesn’t depend on a network or API keys.

Factors we considered

  • Privacy: no accounts, with data stored only in the browser. The profile validates the name field and rejects email-style input.
  • Accessibility: a skip-to-content link, reduced-motion support, touch controls and responsive layouts from 360px to 1920px wide.
  • Reliability: corrupt saved data is recovered gracefully, and certificates can’t be spoofed.
  • Scientific honesty: an educational disclaimer and clear model boundaries. ANANTRA is an independent project, not endorsed by NASA.
  • Quality: per our QA report, 73 automated tests, a clean production build, zero known production vulnerabilities and a 72-check cross-device browser audit.
  • Performance: route-level lazy loading, with the PDF engine loaded only on demand.
